title: भिखारी कविता संग्रहका कवितामा अलङ्कारविधान {Alankaravidhana in the poems of the collection of Bhikhari poems}
nepali: यस लेखमा भिखारी कवितासङ्ग्रहका कवितामा अलङ्कारविधानको निरूपण गरिएको छ । भिखारी कवितासङ्ग्रह लक्ष्मीप्रसाद देवकोटाका १९९२ सालदेखि २००९ सालसम्म विभिन्न पत्रपत्रिकामा प्रकाशित फुटकर कविताको सङ्गृहीत पुस्तकाकार कृति रहेको छ । प्रस्तुत कृतिमा बाईस कविता सङ्कलित रहेका छन् । नेपाली कविताको आधुनिककालीन सन्दर्भको विवेचनाका साथै स्वतन्त्र अध्ययनका क्रममा यस कवितासङ्ग्रहका कविताको विधा सैद्धान्तिक, प्रवृत्तिपरक, मूल्यनिर्णयात्मक तथा वैचारिक अध्ययनका क्रममा उल्लेख भए पनि संस्कृतकाव्य चिन्तन अन्तर्गत अलङ्ककारविधानका कोणबाट हुन नसकेको रिक्तताको परिपूर्तिमा यो लेख केन्द्रित रहेको छ ।संस्कृत काव्यचिन्तन अन्तर्गत अलङ्करविधानलाई सिद्धान्तका रूपमा चयन गरिएको यस लेखका यस कृतिमा प्रकाशित कवितामा शब्दालङ्कार र अर्थालङ्कारको अध्ययन भएको छ । मूलभूत रूपमा अध्ययनका क्रममा यस कवितासङ्ग्रहभित्र अनुप्रास, र यसका छेकानुप्रास, वृत्यानुप्रास, श्रुत्यानुप्रास तथा रूपम तथा अर्थालङ्ककारमध्ये सादृश्यमूलक अर्थालङ्कारका रूपमा उपमा, उत्प्रेक्षा, प्रतिवस्तुपमा, दृष्टान्त, स्मरण र व्यतिरेक, व्यतिरेकमूलक अलङ्कारका रूपमा प्रश्नोत्तर, विरोध,उक्तिचातुर्यमूलक अलङ्ककारका रूपमा परिकर तथा न्यायमूलक अलङ्कार काव्यलिङ्गको उपस्थिति तुलनात्मक रूपले सघन रहेको छ । प्रस्तुत लेखमा संस्कृत काव्यचिन्तनले स्थापित गरेका अलङ्कार विषयक सिद्धान्तका आधारमा भिखारी कवितासङ्ग्रहमा सङ्गृहीत कविताको विश्लेषण गरी निष्कर्ष निकालिएको छ ।
american_english: In this article, the scheme of poetic figures (alankaravidhana) in the poems of the poetry collection 'Bhikhari' is elucidated. The poetry collection 'Bhikhari' is a book-length work compiling standalone poems by Laxmi Prasad Devkota published in various periodicals from 1992 BS to 2009 BS. Twenty-two poems are collected in the present work. Although the poems of this poetry collection have been mentioned during genre-theoretical, trend-oriented, evaluative, and ideological studies alongside discussions of the modern context of Nepali poetry as well as in independent studies, this article focuses on filling the void left unaddressed from the angle of the scheme of figures of speech under Sanskrit poetic thought. In this article, in which the scheme of figures of speech under Sanskrit poetic thought is chosen as the theoretical framework, verbal figures of speech (shabdalamkara) and figures of speech of sense (arthalamkara) in the poems published in this work are studied. Fundamentally, in the course of the study, the presence within this poetry collection of alliteration (anuprasa)—and its varieties chekanuprasa, vrittyanuprasa, shrutyanuprasa, and rupam—as well as, among figures of sense, upama, utpreksha, prativastupama, drishtanta, smarana, and vyatireka as similarity-based figures, prashnottara and virodha as contrast-based figures, parikara as a cleverness-of-expression figure, and kavyalinga as a logic-based figure, is comparatively dense. In the present article, conclusions are drawn by analyzing the poems collected in the poetry collection 'Bhikhari' on the basis of principles regarding figures of speech established by Sanskrit poetic thought.

informal_english: In this article, the setup of poetic figures (alankaravidhana) across the poems in the collection 'Bhikhari' is broken down. The collection 'Bhikhari' is a book-length compilation of standalone poems by Laxmi Prasad Devkota that ran in various periodicals from 1992 BS to 2009 BS. There are twenty-two poems pulled together in this book. Even though the poems in this collection have been brought up in genre-theoretical, trend-based, evaluative, and ideological studies along with discussions of modern Nepali poetry and independent research, this article focuses on filling the blank spot that got skipped from the angle of figures of speech in Sanskrit poetics. With the framework of figures of speech from Sanskrit poetics picked as its theory, this article digs into figures of sound (shabdalamkara) and figures of sense (arthalamkara) across the poems in this collection. Basically, throughout the study, you see a pretty heavy concentration of alliteration (anuprasa)—along with chekanuprasa, vrittyanuprasa, shrutyanuprasa, and rupam—plus, among figures of sense, upama, utpreksha, prativastupama, drishtanta, smarana, and vyatireka as similarity-based devices, prashnottara and virodha as contrast devices, parikara as a witty figure, and kavyalinga as a logic-based figure. In this paper, conclusions are drawn by analyzing the poems collected in 'Bhikhari' using the principles of figures of speech established in Sanskrit poetics.
